newsitem.title: INDIA: ICI India to invest 10 bn rupees in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: ICI India to invest 10 bn rupees in 5 yrs.

text.p: ICI India Ltd plans to invest about 10 billion rupees ($279 million) in India in the next five years as part of its expansion plans, a senior company official said on Wednesday.
"We plan to re-focus on the areas where future growth is going to come from," Param Bhargava, ICI India's vice-president (paints), told Reuters.
The company is 51 percent owned by Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc.
"Growth areas will be acrylics, polyurethene, surfactants and performance chemicals (materials used in industries such as tyres and pharmaceuticals)," he said.
Most of the funding for the expansion plans would come from internal company accruals, at least in the short-term, Bhargava added.
The investment was part of the firm's plans to raise its turnover about tenfold by the year 2005, he said.
In the six months ending September 1996, ICI India's sales totalled 3.06 billion rupees ($85 million), compared to 2.82 billion in the same period a year earlier.

Peter Kirby, the chief executive of ICI Paints, one of the main areas of ICI Plc, in an interview with Reuters on Tuesday said ICI Paints remained bullish towards Asia as quite a few countries continued to show strong growth.
He said ICI India had chalked out rapid expansion plans.
"The growth strategy of ICI India is based on a very major expansion of the paints business here," Kirby said at the opening of a new paints factory at Thane, a town on Bombay's northern outskirts.
Presently, paints contribute about 40-42 percent of the firm's total turnover. Company officials said they planned to increase it to about around 50 percent in the next few years.
The other businesses of ICI India include explosives, chemicals and polyurethene.
ICI's Bhargava said the company's bulk explosive plant at Rourkela in the eastern state of Orrisa is likely to be commissioned in the next few weeks. He did not give any details. ($1=35.8 rupees)
